newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fan mail to Australian mass murderer intercepted.
newsitem.headline: Fan mail to Australian mass murderer intercepted.

text.p: Australian prison guards have intercepted fan mail to Port Arthur mass murderer Martin Bryant from a group of prisoners in another jail.

Queensland state police minister Russell Cooper told reporters on Thursday that warders found a letter addressed to Bryant while making a routine check in a Brisbane correctional centre on Wednesday. The letter, initialled by four prisoners, praised Bryant and expressed a wish to "out do" him, he said.

Charges against the prisoners of threatening violence were possible but it would depend on the wording of the letter, police inspector Bob Pease said. Pease expected to receive a copy of the letter later on Thursday.
"It depends on what the letter says as to whether any offence has been committed," Pease said.

Australia on Monday held a national day of mourning on the first anniversary of the country's worst modern-day massacre in which Bryant shot dead 35 people in the ruins of the former penal colony of Port Arthur in the island state of Tasmania.
Bryant, 29, is serving a life sentence for the massacre.
